clinical_divergence_analysis.summary: Same input → different clinical interpretations on coding philosophy.
clinical_divergence_analysis.corti_approach: Split fracture from osteoporosis. S22.089A (traumatic T11-T12 fracture) + M81.0 (osteoporosis without pathological fracture). Conservative: treats fracture as traumatic by default, separates osteoporosis as background.
clinical_divergence_analysis.icoder_approach: Combined pathologic fracture of osteoporosis: M80.08. Aggressive: given T-score -3.2 (severe osteoporosis), infers the fracture is pathologic, not traumatic.
clinical_divergence_analysis.coding_systems: Corti uses ICD-10-CM (US); iCoDer uses ICD-10-CN (China, 37,897 codes). Code structure differs at subdivision level.
clinical_divergence_analysis.clinical_correctness: Both are defensible. iCoDer is more clinically insightful (pathologic fracture aligns with severe osteoporosis). Corti is more conservative (waits for explicit documentation). Manual review should decide.
clinical_divergence_analysis.common_ground: Both correctly identified hypertension (I10) as secondary.
